sections.text: Fourteen trials test BCMA CAR-T in myasthenia gravis, with one in Phase 3, two in Phase 2, and eleven in Phase 1.
Thirteen of the fourteen trials are currently running, and one was withdrawn before enrolling any participants.
Trials are sponsored by multiple institutions and companies, including Cartesian Therapeutics, Gilead, and academic centers.
A 2026 phase 2b randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial showed that Descartes-08 significantly improved the MG Composite score at month 3 compared to placebo.
The same trial reported that 66.7% of Descartes-08 recipients achieved a ≥5-point improvement in MGC score at month 3, versus 27.3% on placebo, with sustained improvement through month 12.

Recent literature from 2025–2026 highlights durable clinical improvement and favorable safety in refractory MG patients treated with BCMA CAR-T therapies, including minimal toxicity and no severe cytokine release syndrome.
The median trial stop risk for BCMA CAR-T in MG is estimated at 13.7%, based on nine running trials.
Descartes-08 has demonstrated efficacy in an outpatient setting without lymphodepletion, differentiating it from conventional CAR-T approaches.

read: Mechanism evidence: Strong, with positive Phase 2b results and consistent literature support for BCMA CAR-T in refractory MG.
Competitive position: Favorable, due to durable responses, outpatient administration, and no need for lymphodepletion.
Open questions: Long-term safety beyond 12 months and applicability to non-refractory MG populations.
would_change: New long-term safety data showing severe adverse events beyond 12 months would change this judgement.
Failure of the Phase 3 trial (NCT06799247) to replicate efficacy would weaken the stance.
